name: Jon Stewart
role: American comedian and television host (The Daily Show, 1999–2015; 2024–present); 9/11 responders and veterans' health advocate
summary: Stewart is a satirist whose commentary leans liberal-left: he has backed single-payer health care, same-sex marriage, gun background checks and criticised the Roberts Court, Trump's tariffs and Pentagon spending. He has also criticised partisan cable news and, in 2026, pushed back on abolishing prisons and borders. His public record is mostly commentary and advocacy rather than policy programmes, so many topics have no stated position.

universal-healthcare.rationale: On The Daily Show in 2013 he questioned staying with a market-based approach to health coverage and asked why the government would not create a single-payer system.

limit-guns.rationale: Said he is not against the Second Amendment and does not want to ban guns, but backed background checks and registration and attacked loosening gun laws.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2013 he argued the Supreme Court should rule marriage equality right, fair and just under the Constitution, saying rights need no beta-testing, and called DOMA discriminatory.

abortion-legal.rationale: After Roe was overturned he said the decision was not based on reasoned debate and contrasted states being barred from regulating guns while free to regulate abortion; he did not state a detailed abortion policy.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In 2025 he called Trump's tariffs reckless and recalled the Great Depression, saying trade problems are mostly homegrown; he allowed that deals could be renegotiated.

empower-police-military.rationale: Criticised the Pentagon getting a raise after 20 years of war and spending priorities favouring contractors over troops; he did not speak to police authority in these remarks, and later said order and security are also a progressive value.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Complained that Supreme Court rulings mean agencies 'no longer have the ability to regulate anything' and that the Court enabled financial corruption (2026).

corporate-influence.rationale: Criticised Citizens United and said Court decisions made the country subject to 'financial corruption' (the Citizens United point is the reporter's paraphrase).

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Became vegetarian and then vegan for ethical reasons, runs a farm animal sanctuary, and said it is harder to eat meat when you know the animal's name.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In his 2024 Gaza monologue he said he wants a 'safe and free Israel' alongside a safe and free Palestine; his focus was ceasefire and ending the cycle of violence.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: In 2026 he told Mayor Mamdani he does not think abolishing all prisons is a good idea and said order and security are also a progressive value.

open-borders.rationale: In 2026 he said he does not think abolishing all borders is a good idea.

cut-welfare.rationale: His 2021 episode on the working-class economy criticised bailouts for the wealthy being accepted while aid to ordinary people is labelled socialism; per an episode summary, not a direct statement on welfare dependency.

notes: Commentary comes mainly from comedy broadcasts, where satire can blur sincere positions; only clear statements were used. Many reports are secondary summaries of his remarks.
